02

Persistent text data

Use a with block, select the correct mode and keep the Python file beside its supporting data files.

01

Open and close safely

A with block opens the file and closes it automatically when the indented block ends.

with open("message.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    message = file.read()
print(message)
02

Read line by line

Loop through the file for repeated records. strip() removes the newline from each line.

with open("scores.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    for line in file:
        print(line.strip())
03

Write or append

Mode w replaces the file. Mode a preserves existing content and adds at the end.

with open("log.txt", "a", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write(entry + "\n")
04

Split stored records

A delimiter separates fields. Split the cleaned line, then cast numerical fields.

fields = line.strip().split(",")
name = fields[0]
score = int(fields[1])

File modes and safe errors

ModePurposeMain risk
rRead existing dataFileNotFoundError if the file is missing
wCreate or replace a fileExisting contents are cleared
aAdd to the endA missing newline can join records

Use try and except FileNotFoundError when a missing file needs a clear user message.

    PYTHON LAB REFERENCE
    Support & examples
    Use this reference to check file modes, reading patterns and safe closing.
    Key concepts
    • Use with open(...) so Python closes the file automatically.
    • Mode r reads, w replaces and a adds to the end.
    • read() returns all text; a loop processes one line at a time.
    • Strip the newline before splitting a stored record.
    • Keep the data file in the same project folder unless a different path is required.
    Common errors
    • Using write mode when append was intended
    • Forgetting the newline when adding a record
    • Trying to open a file that is not in the project folder
    • Splitting a line before removing its newline
    Misconceptions to avoid
    Write mode adds new data
    Mode w clears the existing contents before writing. Use a to preserve existing records.
    close() is always needed
    A with block closes the file automatically, including when an error interrupts the block.
    EXAMPLE 01 · READ
    Read every line
    with open("scores.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    for line in file:
        print(line.strip())
    strip() removes the stored newline before display.
    EXAMPLE 02 · APPEND
    Add one record
    with open("members.txt", "a", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write(name + "\n")
    The newline keeps the next record on a separate line.
    EXAMPLE 03 · SPLIT
    Decode a record
    fields = line.strip().split(",")
name = fields[0]
score = int(fields[1])
    Split text fields, then cast numerical data when needed.
